title: Impulse Buying
description: Buying something immediately without thinking about whether you actually need it.
scenario: A student receives their monthly allowance and immediately buys new shoes because they are on sale. A few days later, they don't have enough money for transportation and food.
action: Wait before making non-essential purchases. Give yourself 24 hours to decide whether you really need the item.

title: Ignoring Small Expenses
description: Small daily purchases can seem harmless, but they can add up to a large amount over a month.
scenario: A student spends ₦1,000 on snacks and drinks almost every day. By the end of the month, they have spent around ₦30,000 without realizing it.
action: Track your small daily expenses. Set a weekly limit for snacks, drinks, and other small purchases.

title: Late Payments
description: Forgetting bills or paying them late can result in additional charges and unnecessary financial stress.
scenario: A student forgets to renew an important service before the due date and has to pay an extra fee to restore it.
action: Keep track of payment dates. Use reminders on your phone or calendar so you know when payments are due.

title: Unused Subscriptions
description: Paying for subscriptions you rarely or never use wastes money that could be used for more important goals.
scenario: A student subscribes to several streaming and learning platforms but only uses one of them. The unused subscriptions continue taking money every month.
action: Review your subscriptions every month and cancel services you no longer use.

title: Spending Without a Plan
description: Spending money without deciding where it should go can make it difficult to control your finances.
scenario: A student receives ₦100,000 but starts spending immediately without setting aside money for food, transportation, school expenses, or savings.
action: Create a simple spending plan before using your income. Decide how much goes toward needs, wants, and savings.
